summary: The Heidelberg Catechism, which the Reformed Church in America holds as one of its standards, teaches that a person is righteous before God only by true faith in Jesus Christ: God, without any merit of the person but of mere grace, grants and counts to them the perfect satisfaction, righteousness and holiness of Christ, as though they had never sinned and had fully obeyed. The catechism explains that faith is not the ground of acceptance, since only Christ's satisfaction is, and that faith is the only way the person can receive it. The questions read do not address election in the sense of God's eternal choice or whether believers can fall away.

points.question: How are you righteous before God?
points.answer: Only by true faith in Jesus Christ: God, without any merit of ours but of mere grace, grants and counts to us the perfect satisfaction, righteousness and holiness of Christ, as if we had never sinned, when we receive it with a believing heart.

points.question: Why say "by faith only"?
points.answer: Not because faith is worthy in itself, but because only Christ's satisfaction, righteousness and holiness is our righteousness before God, and faith is the only way we can receive and apply it.
